sentence: This project develops imaging markers for each patient that show early disease in cervical spinal cord compression.
This project tests whether antibodies that neutralize a circulating protein can improve bone fracture healing in aged individuals.
This project tries to find out why people with HIV who are aging get brain disease, heart disease and cancer at higher rates.
This project studies how social networks and daily interpersonal processes are linked to hearing aid use among older adults.
This project studies how a germ cell becomes an oocyte that supplies maternal RNAs and proteins, using Drosophila as a model system.
This project builds a research partnership with community partners to pursue cancer research.
This project develops technology to study bacterial genes and their functions and how the immune system reacts to different pathogens.
This project studies how bacterial cells in a biofilm sense and respond to the shear forces of fluid flow.
This project compares gene expression in arterial endothelial cells made from human, chimpanzee and human-chimpanzee hybrid cells to learn about atherosclerosis.
This project tries to find out how trachea-esophageal birth defects develop.
This project studies how T-cell receptor signaling links to resistance to apoptosis in T cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma, to find treatment strategies.
This project develops a simple office device that checks for obstructed fallopian tubes without imaging or referral to a specialist.
This project uses a chemical method to modify immune cells so they can target and eliminate cancer cells.
This project supports organoid models and biomarker analysis to study a serious complication of stem cell transplantation.
This project runs collaborative research programs that aim to accelerate the prevention and treatment of cancer.
This project studies how bacterial pathways that make androgen in the gut contribute to treatment resistance in metastatic prostate cancer.
This project studies how plasma cells reach a long-lived state in the bone marrow and the gut lamina propria.
This project uses stem cells from Alzheimer's disease patients to study what makes tau and amyloid-beta oligomers toxic.
This project studies how gut bacteria promote tissue regeneration by regulating vitamin A metabolism and T-cell responses.
This project develops a method to read the amino acid sequence of single protein molecules through nanopores.
